content.comment_body: I am experiencing an issue with my [product_name] device. Every time there is an electric storm, the program in the [product_name] seems to change. How can I prevent this from happening?

Hello [user_name], can you clarify what you mean by "the program changes"? Normally, the program should not alter itself. It is possible that functions like timers or counters are resetting to zero when there is a voltage drop or power supply issue. Try enabling retentivity for these features. If you can, please share your program along with a detailed description of the issue.
I installed a UPS on my [product_name] devices and haven't experienced any such problems.

That solution might be a bit costly. Consider protecting the power supply to the [product_name] device as recommended in the manual, and perhaps use a UPS or battery setup with a charger and buffer circuitry appropriate for 12 or 24V DC models.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report unexpected changes in the [product_name] program during electric storms, suspected to be due to power supply disturbances. Other participants mention program corruption is rare, instead suggesting certain features like timers or counters may lose retention when power drops. Recommendations include enabling retention for critical functions and ensuring the power supply is stable, possibly with backup or buffering solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the [product_name] program to remain unchanged and retain its settings, even during and after electric storms or power fluctuations.
